title: S3M3D: Cross-Modal Selective State Space Modulation for 3D Object Detection
primary_area: unsupervised, self-supervised, semi-supervised, and supervised representation learning

response.summary: The paper proposes S3M3D, combining Z-order-serialized bidirectional Mamba processing for LiDAR queries with a state-space module whose parameters are conditioned jointly on LiDAR and camera queries. The design is plausible and produces consistent gains on nuScenes, but the novelty is incremental and the evidence does not adequately isolate the claimed asymmetric-guidance mechanism or establish robustness to camera uncertainty.
strengths: The method is clearly motivated and technically specified, including serialization, bidirectional/orthogonal scans, and conditional SSM equations (pp. 4–7).
Matched ablations show both modules contribute, with the combined model improving the VoVNet baseline from 70.3/73.1 to 71.1/73.7 mAP/NDS (p. 8).
The paper reports validation and test results plus limited latency analysis; S3M3D reaches 71.2 mAP and 73.6 NDS on the nuScenes test set (pp. 7–9).
weaknesses: The main LiDAR-only comparison is substantially confounded by the backbone: the headline 63.7-to-67.0 mAP gain contrasts FUTR3D with an HEDNet-based model, while the matched HEDNet ablation attributes only 0.4 mAP and 0.3 NDS to SA-Mamba (pp. 7–9).

The central asymmetric-fusion claim is insufficiently isolated: the dynamic SSM parameters are generated from an additive mixture of camera and LiDAR projections, and there are no comparisons against simpler LiDAR-conditioned gates/cross-attention or alternative asymmetric fusion designs (p. 6).

Evidence is limited to one benchmark and lacks experiments under calibration errors, camera corruption, missing sensors, or adverse conditions—the settings needed to support claims about projection uncertainty and robustness; serialization alternatives and statistical variation are also absent (pp. 7–9).
response.score_rationale: The approach is coherent and yields reproducible-looking but modest matched gains. However, limited novelty over established Mamba serialization/conditioning, confounded headline comparisons, and missing robustness and mechanism-specific controls leave the central claims under-supported. I therefore rate it marginally below acceptance, with some uncertainty because implementation details and repeated-run variance are unavailable.

response.summary: S3M3D replaces LiDAR-query self-attention with bidirectional Mamba over orthogonal Z-order serializations and conditions camera-query state-space parameters on aligned LiDAR and camera queries. The design is coherent and improves a FUTR3D-based detector on nuScenes, but the evidence does not adequately isolate the claimed advantages of spatial serialization and asymmetric fusion.
strengths: The two modules form a clear, technically plausible pipeline: SA-Mamba structures LiDAR queries, while LG-Mamba uses aligned LiDAR features to modulate camera-query processing (pp. 4–7).
Component ablations across two camera backbones show consistent improvements, with the combined model performing best, and basic latency/FPS measurements are provided (pp. 8–9, Tables 2–4).
The reported nuScenes results are competitive: 71.2 mAP/73.6 NDS on the test set and improvements over the stated FUTR3D baseline (pp. 7–8, Table 1).
weaknesses: The novelty is incremental—primarily applying established Mamba scans and Morton/Z-order serialization to object queries—and the claim that self-attention cannot capture spatial arrangement is overstated because query features can encode reference-point position (pp. 1, 3–6).

The central asymmetric-fusion hypothesis is insufficiently tested: there is no controlled comparison against equally parameterized symmetric fusion, cross-attention, or simple LiDAR-conditioned gating, and no projection-noise, sensor-corruption, adverse-weather, or missing-modality evaluation (pp. 5–9).

Evidence is narrow and potentially confounded. Results cover only nuScenes; the large LiDAR gain against FUTR3D partly reflects switching to HEDNet (the controlled gain is only 0.4 mAP/0.3 NDS), while several key gains are 0.2–0.6 points without seeds or uncertainty estimates (pp. 7–9, Tables 1–4).
response.score_rationale: The method is coherent and empirically promising, but the modest novelty and missing controls for its main causal claims place it marginally below acceptance. It is uncertain whether the small controlled gains exceed run-to-run variation or arise specifically from asymmetric state-space modulation rather than added capacity and conditioning.

response.summary: S3M3D replaces LiDAR-query self-attention with bidirectional Z-order Mamba scans and conditions camera-query SSM parameters on aligned LiDAR queries. The design is plausible and yields modest nuScenes gains, but the evidence does not isolate the claimed benefits of asymmetric guidance or establish robustness to camera uncertainty.
strengths: The combination of spatial serialization for sparse queries and LiDAR-conditioned SSM parameters is coherent and moderately novel; the mechanism is described with equations and architectural diagrams (pp. 4–7).
Component ablations across two camera backbones show consistent gains, with the full model reaching 71.1 mAP/73.7 NDS on validation (pp. 8–9).
The paper reports scan overhead, latency, and a naive Bi-Mamba control, supporting the importance of spatial ordering and showing low runtime overhead (pp. 8–9).
weaknesses: The central asymmetric-fusion claim is weakly validated: there are no controls for reversed guidance, symmetric Mamba fusion, concatenation/gating with comparable capacity, or controlled camera corruption. LG-Mamba improves the strong VoVNet baseline by only 0.4 mAP/0.4 NDS alone (pp. 8–9).

Evaluation is confined to nuScenes and lacks adverse-weather, calibration-error, missing-modality, or projection-noise tests, despite robustness to camera uncertainty being a primary motivation (pp. 1, 5, 7–9).

SA-Mamba reuses permutations computed from initial reference points even though points are iteratively updated, potentially making later-layer ordering stale; this choice is asserted rather than analyzed. Parameter counts/FLOPs and variance across runs are also absent (pp. 3–5, 8).
response.score_rationale: The method is technically plausible and achieves consistent but mostly modest improvements, including +0.6 NDS over the reported VoVNet baseline on validation and +1.5 NDS over FUTR3D on test (pp. 7–9). However, missing directional/fusion controls and robustness experiments leave the main causal claims under-supported, placing it marginally below acceptance. Uncertainty remains because implementation details and repeated-run statistics are not provided.

response.summary: S3M3D replaces LiDAR-query self-attention with spatially serialized Mamba scans and conditions camera-query state-space parameters on aligned LiDAR features. The design is plausible and yields consistent nuScenes improvements, but the strongest claims about asymmetric robustness and state-of-the-art performance are not adequately isolated or tested.
strengths: The combination of recursive orthogonal Z-order scans and LiDAR-conditioned SSM parameters is a coherent, moderately novel adaptation of Mamba to sparse multimodal object queries (pp. 4–7).
Component ablations show consistent gains from SA-Mamba and LG-Mamba across two camera backbones, with the combined model performing best (pp. 8–9).
The paper reports validation and test results, per-class AP, latency breakdowns, and comparisons against several established nuScenes detectors (pp. 7–9).
weaknesses: The main comparison is confounded by architecture and training changes: S3M3D uses HEDNet and a two-stage initialization scheme, while Table 1 compares primarily to reported FUTR3D results; the controlled VoVNet ablation shows only a 0.6 NDS gain for the full model (pp. 7–9).

The central robustness motivation is weakly evidenced: there are no calibration-noise, adverse-weather, modality-dropout, depth-uncertainty, or broader-dataset tests, and no statistical variation is reported (pp. 7–9).

The method reuses permutations across decoder layers even though reference points are iteratively updated, potentially making the claimed spatial ordering stale; this choice is neither justified nor ablated (pp. 3–5).
response.score_rationale: The method is technically plausible and empirically improves its controlled baseline, but novelty is incremental and the decisive gains are modest. Confounded headline comparisons, limited evaluation on only nuScenes, and the unexamined stale-ordering issue leave the evidence slightly below the acceptance bar.

response.summary: The paper proposes a plausible Mamba-based decoder for multimodal 3D detection: SA-Mamba serializes LiDAR queries using two Z-order scans, while LG-Mamba uses aligned LiDAR features to condition the state-space processing of camera queries. Results on nuScenes are positive but modest, and the experiments do not adequately isolate the claimed advantages of spatial serialization and asymmetric fusion.
strengths: The method is coherent and reasonably well specified, with complementary spatial serialization and LiDAR-conditioned camera processing (pp. 4–7).
Controlled ablations show consistent improvements over attention or naive bidirectional Mamba, with little change in end-to-end FPS (pp. 8–9, Tables 2–4).
The full model reports competitive nuScenes validation/test performance, including 71.2 mAP and 73.6 NDS on the test set (pp. 7–8, Table 1).
weaknesses: Evidence is limited to one dataset and lacks the tests most relevant to the central claims: symmetric-fusion alternatives, random/Hilbert/other spatial orderings, calibration or projection perturbations, sensor degradation, and adverse-weather robustness (pp. 7–9).

The novelty is incremental: it combines established Mamba selective scans, bidirectionality, and space-filling-curve serialization with query fusion; moreover, the claim that self-attention is inherently spatially agnostic is overstated because positional/reference-point information can be incorporated (pp. 1, 3–6).

Some conclusions exceed the ablations. The claimed synergy is weak or sub-additive in parts of Table 3, and comparisons in Table 1 are potentially confounded by backbone/training changes; the paper also reuses fixed permutations despite iterative reference-point updates without analyzing stale spatial order (pp. 5, 7–9).
response.score_rationale: The approach is technically plausible and yields consistent gains, but the improvements are modest and the experimental design does not convincingly establish that asymmetric LiDAR guidance or Z-order serialization—not implementation and training choices—causes them. Given the limited robustness analysis and incremental novelty, this is marginally below acceptance.
